name: Pick a Partner Poker
description: Pick a Partner is a stud poker variant for an even number of players. Everyone antes and receives five cards face down. All players simultaneously expose one card (roll). The highest card holder picks a partner; then the highest unpartnered player picks, until all are paired. Each partnership combines their eight remaining cards and selects three to use with their two upcards to form a five-card hand. Three betting rounds follow, with one of the three chosen cards turned face up after each round. Partners bet as individuals; the team with the best hand shares the pot, or one partner wins the whole pot if the other folded.

history.origins: Pick a Partner is a stud poker variant from the Roll Your Own family. It combines ante, a simultaneous card expose (roll) for partner selection, and partnership hand formation with multiple betting rounds and gradual card reveals.
timeline: 20th century: Stud poker variant in the Roll Your Own family; partner selection by exposed card rank.

setup.dealing: Each player antes. Dealer deals five cards face down to each player. All players simultaneously expose one card (roll). Highest card holder selects a partner; then the highest unpartnered player selects a partner, and so on until all are paired. Each partnership combines their eight remaining cards and selects three to use with their two upcards to form a five-card hand. Three betting rounds follow, with one of the three chosen cards turned face up after each round.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best five-card poker hand at showdown as a partnership, or by being the last partnership with a member still in the hand. If one member of the winning partnership folded, the remaining partner wins the whole pot.
rules.gameplay: After ante and deal, all players roll one card simultaneously. Partner selection proceeds by rank of the exposed card: highest picks first, then highest unpartnered, until all are paired. Each partnership combines their eight remaining cards and selects three to use with their two upcards to form a five-card hand. There are three betting rounds; after each round one of the three chosen cards is turned face up. Partners play as a team but bet as individuals: if one folds the other may continue. At showdown the team with the highest hand shares the pot; if one partner folded, the other wins the whole pot.
keyRules: Even number of players only. Everyone antes and is dealt five cards face down.
Roll is simultaneous: everyone selects and exposes one card at once.
Partner selection order is by rank of exposed card, highest first.
Partnership combines eight cards and selects three to use with two upcards for a five-card hand.
Three betting rounds with one card revealed after each round.
Partners bet individually; one partner can fold while the other continues.
Winning team shares pot; if one winner folded, the other wins the whole pot.

strategy.basic: Coordinate with partner on which three cards to select from your combined eight; consider saving strong cards for later reveals. In the roll phase, exposing a high card gives your side first choice of partner.

scoring.winCondition: Partnership with the best five-card poker hand at showdown wins and shares the pot; if one member of the winning partnership folded, the remaining partner wins the whole pot.
